beats.say: This time the scam comes by phone: a fake bank security team calls you.
They say your card is stolen and you must move money to a safe account.
There is no such safe account, and no bank asks you to install an app.
End the call and dial the number on the back of your card yourself.

nodes.text: There is a suspicious payment on your card. We must move the money to a safe account.
nodes.speaker: SahilBank security
nodes.spoken: There is a suspicious payment on your card. <breath> We must move the money to a safe account.

choices.label: I end the call and dial the number on the back of my card myself
choices.feedback: Correct. The only way to check is to find the number yourself and call.

choices.label: I give my card details so they can check
choices.feedback: A real bank does not ask for your card number or code. With this they empty your account.

choices.label: I install the app they ask for
choices.feedback: The app hands them your phone. A bank never asks you to install such an app.

nodes.text: We did not send any such warning.
nodes.speaker: Bank operator (number on the back of your card)
nodes.spoken: We did not send <breath> any such warning.

choices.label: I report the call and the suspicious number
choices.feedback: Great. The bank can now watch your account and warn others too.

choices.label: I do not worry, it was probably a mistake
choices.feedback: The scammer may call again. Telling the bank what happened protects you.

scenes.title: The fake support call
scenes.intro: A call comes in from your bank. Read what the caller says and choose your answer each time.

actions.label: Answer
actions.feedback: Answering itself is not dangerous. What matters is that you give nothing away.

actions.label: Decline
actions.feedback: That works too. Then call the number on the back of your card yourself.

steps.say: Hello, this is Tural from SahilBank security. Twelve hundred manat, excuse me, was taken from your card.
steps.spoken: Hello, <breath> this is Tural from SahilBank security. Twelve hundred manat <cough> excuse me, was taken from your card.

actions.label: I listen but say nothing
actions.feedback: Good. You may listen, as long as you give no information.

actions.label: End the call
actions.feedback: Right choice. A bank does not call like this, so ending it is correct.

steps.say: A code just arrived on your phone to confirm. Please read that code to me.
steps.spoken: A code just arrived on your phone to confirm. <breath> Please read that code to me.

actions.label: I do not read the code
actions.feedback: Correct. The code that arrives is the key to your account, never tell it to anyone.

actions.label: I read the code
actions.feedback: The moment you read it out, they get into your account. A bank never asks for this code.

steps.say: So I can help you, please install the UzaqMasa app and let me connect.
steps.spoken: So I can help you, uh, please install the UzaqMasa app and <breath> let me connect.

actions.label: I do not install the app
actions.feedback: Correct. You never install a remote access app because a caller asks you to.

actions.label: Install the app
actions.feedback: Now the caller sees your screen and controls your phone. Never install such an app.

steps.label: The call has ended. What do you do now?

actions.label: Call the number on the back of the card
actions.feedback: Correct. The bank will confirm the call was fake and check your account.

actions.label: Call back the number that called
actions.feedback: That number goes to the scammer again. Only take the number from your card.

actions.label: Do nothing
actions.feedback: The scammer may try again. To be safe, call the bank yourself.

scenes.prompt: Put the steps in order when a call like this claims to be the bank.

items.label: Find the number on the back of your card

scenes.explain: This is the only way to check: end the call and dial the number you found yourself.

question.prompt: You already installed the help app the caller asked for. What do you do now?

options.label: I disconnect, tell tech support and call the bank myself
options.feedback: Correct. Disconnecting stops the connection, then asking for help is the right move.

options.label: I keep the app, maybe I will need it
options.feedback: While the app stays, they control your phone. Disconnect and remove it at once.

options.label: I wait, since nothing happened
options.feedback: Waiting adds to the harm. The sooner you report it, the more you can save.

scenes.explain: If the app is already there, disconnect at once, tell tech support and call the bank on the number on your card.

points: There is no such thing as a safe account
Do not install an app because a caller asks
End the call and dial the number on your card yourself
